sector_model: Card issuer and payments network with bank funding: credit costs, net write-off rates, delinquency, funding (deposits and long term debt), CET1, ROE, regulatory exposure; not a generic industrial and FCF is secondary to earnings and capital.
thesis: American Express (NYSE: AXP). Q3 2026 10-Q (0000004962-26-000409, filed 2026-10-23): revenue net of interest expense 20,062M +9% (9M 58,606M +10%); net income 3,712M +28% (9M 9,794M +17%); diluted EPS 5.42 vs 4.14 (9M 14.22 vs 11.85). Q3 includes a 982M pretax (751M after tax, 1.11/share) gain on GBTG equity sale and a 336M pretax (253M after tax, 0.37/share) restructuring charge, net about +498M after tax, so underlying Q3 NI is about 3.21B. Credit: Q3 provisions 985M vs 1,287M (reserve release); net write-off rate principal, interest and fees 2.1% vs 2.2%; 30+ days past due consumer and small business 1.2% vs 1.3%. Card balances 221.1B +7%; deposits 155.0B; long term debt 58.5B; cash 43.2B vs 54.7B a year ago; total assets 310.3B, liabilities 274.5B, equity 35.8B. ROE 42.4% Q3, 38.0% 9M; CET1 10.9% (target 10 to 11%). 8-K 2026-10-08: AENB consented to an OCC order with a 350M civil money penalty (part reserved earlier), Federal Reserve order for the parent, no asset cap, no expected effect on 2026 or 2027 guidance (per 8-K text read). TTM NI (FY2025 10,833M + 9M26 9,794M - 9M25 8,371M) = 12,256M; shares 670,552,018 (cover 2026-10-15); close 320.60 gives market cap 215.0B, 17.5x TTM reported (about 18.3x if the net 498M one-off gain is removed from Q3 only, approximate), 6.0x book, dividend 0.95 quarterly (yield about 1.2%). 9M buybacks 5,805M. TTM operating cash flow 17,626M less PP&E capex 3,716M = 13.9B (6.5% of market cap), but for a lender operating cash flow includes financing-like working capital, so P/E, ROE and credit are the primary lenses. Market view: premium franchise earning a high return with a closed loop network; price assumes ROE near high 30s persists and credit stays benign. Evidence for: growth near 10%, falling write-offs, CET1 at target. Peer update 2026-11-16 (stockanalysis.com, 2026-11-13 closes, one aggregator origin): AXP is about 17.5x trailing against V 34.8x (fwd 28.3, ROE 63.5%) and MA 34.6x (fwd 29.7); COF 11.6x trailing, 8.5x forward, 1.12x book, ROE 9.4%. AXP sits between the network duopoly and the lender, consistent with a hybrid; no clear relative discount.
counterthesis: Valuation is 17.5x earnings at 6x book on a 38% ROE, so the price already pays for peak-like returns; the Q3 EPS jump of 31% is flattered by the reserve release and net one-off gains. Provisions fell 23% while 9M write-offs rose, so credit benefit may reverse in a downturn. Customer rewards and engagement expense growth is the main cost lever (management says growth will moderate next quarter). Funding relies on 155B deposits and 58.5B debt; cash is down 11.5B y/y. Regulatory: 350M OCC penalty and Fed order over financial crimes compliance (resolved but order compliance costs and any later findings are risk); interchange and CFPB rules (late fee, swipe fee legislation) are tail risks. Rich-income households and millennials are the growth engine and are cyclical. Peers (V, MA, COF, DFS-type issuers) and own-history multiples were not read, 10-Q MD&A was read only in part, and risk factors and 10-K were not read.
invalidation: Thesis fails if net write-off rate and delinquencies rise materially above 2.2% and 1.2%, billed business growth falls below high single digits, ROE drops well below 30%, or regulators restrict growth or capital return.
